name: Safdarjung Tomb Night Heritage Walk
description: Safdarjung’s Tomb Heritage Walkcurated by Darwesh heritage walks in collaboration with Sabhyata Foundation.Join us for a journey into the fading glow of Mughal splendour at Safdarjung's Tomb — often called the *last flicker of Mughal grandeur* in Delhi.Built in 1754 for Safdarjung, the powerful Nawab of Awadh and Prime Minister of the Mughal court, this monument stands at the twilight of an empire — grand in ambition, yet carrying within it the quiet signs of decline.Its story is as fascinating as its form. From courtly intrigues and shifting loyalties to the architectural choices that reveal a changing political landscape, Safdarjung’s life opens a compelling window into 18th-century Delhi.We will also trace a lesser-known layer of its history — how this tomb was constructed by reusing material from a pre-existing Mughal structure, quite literally building one memory over another.To truly understand Delhi — its rise, its resilience, and its gradual transitions — a visit to Safdarjung’s Tomb is essential.Come, walk with us through the final chapter of Mughal architectural brilliance — where grandeur meets gravity, and history lingers in every arch.

name: Grounds For Thought: August Lineup
description: Grounds for Thought: August 2026A Blue Tokai × unLecture SeriesFour Thursday evenings. Four very different conversations. Grounds for Thought is a monthly series where Blue Tokai and unLecture bring researchers, scientists, and thinkers out of their institutions and into a coffee shops. The format is simple: an expert, a room full of curious people, and a conversation that goes somewhere a classroom rarely does.6th August: Shambhavi TiwariPossessed: The Ghost, The Asylum, The Priest, and the PeopleWhen someone in rural India is "possessed by a ghost," they encounter not just their family and their priest, but eventually — often — a psychiatrist. Two completely different frameworks for what has gone wrong, and what healing looks like. This session uses spirit possession across Indian cultural contexts to examine what happens when indigenous knowledge systems and clinical medicine cross paths. PhD researcher Shambhavi Tiwari, who has spent years in this space, asks: superstition, myth, knowledge system, or something else entirely?13th August: Dr. Vishwas ChitaleZoom In, Zoom Out: What India's Climate Risk Looks Like at Ground LevelEveryone has heard the national climate numbers. But zoom into a district, and the picture changes entirely — neighbouring areas with opposite risk profiles, and disaster plans built on averages too coarse to catch where the real danger sits. Dr. Vishwas Chitale, Fellow at CEEW, will walk us through India's climate risk from the national level down to your own neighbourhood — and then hand the tool to the room. Participants will pull up their own hometown's actual climate risk profile live, using CRAVIS, CEEW's climate intelligence platform. You'll leave having done a small piece of the research yourself.20th August: Antara ChakrabartyFrom Village to Viral: How Folk Music Got a Second LifeA seventeenth-century Sufi verse now has a hundred million YouTube views. The songs of Lalon Fakir, Bengal's wandering poet-saint, are uniting two Bengals and two centuries through a single melody. This session traces folk music's remarkable journey — from Punjab's Sufi shrines and Bengal's riverside Baul gatherings to studio stages and streaming platforms — and asks the questions nobody quite wants to answer. Who owns a folk song? What happens when heritage becomes entertainment? Does something get lost in translation, or does it simply learn a new way to survive? Expect live music, a few surprises, and a fresh way of listening to songs you may already love.27th August: Sunaina SaxenaWhat is a Clean Street Worth?Why are two seemingly identical houses priced so differently? This session explores one of environmental economics' most elegant tools, hedonic pricing, to answer a question most of us have never thought to ask: does the cleanliness of a neighbourhood have a measurable economic value? Through stories, discussion, and simple examples, researcher Sunaina Saxena explores how clean streets, reliable waste collection, and a healthy living environment become embedded in housing prices — and what that reveals about our cities and the choices we make about where we live.

name: August Spl : 1857 & Dilli - heritage walk in Ridge
description: 1857 UPRISING & DILLI: (A heritage walk at the Mutiny Memorial & it's neighbourhood in Kamla Nehru Ridge )The year 1857 marked a turning point in Indian history. What began as a sepoy mutiny in Meerut soon transformed into a widespread rebellion against British colonial rule. Within days, the rebelling sepoys marched to Delhi, a city symbolic of imperial power, where they declared the aging Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar as the leader of the uprising.The Mutiny Memorial, now known as Ajitgarh, is a prominent monument located on the Delhi Ridge, near Kashmere Gate. It was constructed in 1863 by the British to honor their soldiers and officials who died during the 1857 uprising.Let’s explore the stories of the 1857 uprising and its impacts, at the Mutiny Memorial (a haunted site ) &  its neighborhood landmarks (Ashokan Pillar, Baoli, Pir Ghaib Hunting Lodge & the Hindu Rao Hospital)

name: The Making of a Serial Offender
description: Join us for an evening that begins with a simple question: what does a serial offender look like? The answer may be more unsettling than you think.About the LectureThe point is not that everyone is a criminal. The point is that none of us can recognise one by looking.This lecture explores how criminal profiling moved beyond outdated assumptions about "criminal faces" to become one of the most fascinating tools in modern investigations. Drawing from forensic psychology, criminology, and real-world case studies, the session examines how investigators attempt to understand offenders through behaviour rather than appearance.Together, we'll explore:Why humans are often poor judges of who is capable of violenceThe evolution of criminal profiling, from early theories to modern investigative psychologyHow crime scene behaviour can reveal patterns of motive, planning, control, and escalationThe origins of behavioural profiling and the rise of the FBI's Behavioural Science UnitWhat famous serial offender cases reveal about fantasy, victim selection, and criminal developmentWhy serial offending remains understudied in IndiaHow forensic psychologists and investigators use Behavioural Evidence Analysis to reconstruct offender behaviourMoving beyond sensationalism and popular crime shows, this lecture examines the deeper psychological and social questions that profiling raises. Why do some individuals cross lines that most never do? What can behaviour tell us about risk, intent, and future offending? And how can India build more rigorous behavioural science frameworks for criminal investigation?Part psychology, part criminology, and part investigative science, this session offers a rare glimpse into the complex process of understanding criminal behaviour.About the SpeakerMr. Rithin Joseph is an Assistant Professor at the School of Behavioural Forensics, National Forensic Sciences University (NFSU), Delhi. Specialising in Criminology and Forensic Psychology, his work focuses on criminal profiling, deception detection, investigative psychology, and forensic behavioural analysis. He has published multiple research papers and presented over twenty-one papers at national and international conferences.Mr. Joseph has specialised training in a range of forensic investigative techniques, including Polygraph, Brain Electrical Oscillation Signature Profiling (BEOS), Suspect Detection System (SDS), Layered Voice Analysis (LVA), and EyeDetect. He currently serves as Co-Investigator on an ICSSR-funded research project examining the prediction of recidivism among first-time offenders in conflict with the law. He is also the co-author of "Crime as the Cause of Criminality" and "BRICS: Unravelling the Abyss."A Gold Medalist in Criminology from the National Forensic Sciences University and recipient of the Young Criminologist Award 2024, he continues to contribute to research in criminal psychology, offender behaviour, and investigative science while mentoring postgraduate students and pursuing doctoral research in Criminal Psychology.About unLectureunLecture brings experts out of classrooms and into cafés, bars and neighbourhood spaces across Delhi. Created by three friends from college who wanted learning to feel warm, social and alive — unLecture turns an otherwise ordinary evening into a conversation you may think about long after it ends.

We look forward to sharing this unforgettable night with you!

name: Level 1 - I LIKE TO MOVE IT MOVE IT! EARLY BIRD
description: I LIKE TO MOVE IT, MOVE IT! Dancing for Non-Dancers is a playful movement and body-awareness practice. It invites you to rediscover movement not as performance or technique, but as a process of curiosity.The programme expands movement vocabulary, deepens mind-body awareness and develops a broader appreciation of what dance can be.Participants leave with a deeper understanding of their bodies and movement patterns, greater responsiveness to music and rhythm and practical tools that support mobility, adaptability, physical wellbeing and long-term vitality.(Warning: Side effects may include increased spontaneity, killer dance moves and unexpected joy.)Every WEDNESDAY (5-7pm) and every SATURDAY (11am-1pm) for the month of SEPTEMBER, 2026Rs. 15,000/- for the month, Level 1 courseEarly bird (till August 20): Rs. 12,000/-(Please click on the 'Sept 2nd 5:00-5:01pm' option for ticket booking - this entitles you to the FULL MONTH of classes)Further details on what we will explore during the course are mentioned below.**ABOUT SHENAShena Gamat is a theatre practitioner, voice artist and learning & development professional with over two decades of experience in performance and facilitation. Her background spans film, international theatre tours and voice work.Shena has built a magazine, run a theatre company, been on leadership teams, built grassroots programmes, created communities and facilitated learning. She is a qualified Movement Therapist and the founder of It’s All Good, an initiative for fun and engaging experiences that foster insight and empowerment.Her sessions combine theatre tools, voice work, learning design and behavioural frameworks to help participants connect to their own presence and live with clarity & confidence.*ABOUT IT’S ALL GOODThe Science and Art of JoyIAG is an initiative aimed at returning to joy in a complex world. IAG offers workshops, talks, performances and micro-festivals that explore the human condition, delving into how to live with ease and clarity (and humour!).Insta : https://www.instagram.com/itsallgood.space*ZAAZEN WELLNESSZaazen is a holistic wellness sanctuary for both men and women. A space designed for anyone seeking to slow down, restore, and reconnect at any stage of life.Reimagined in 2025, Zaazen brings together therapeutic bodywork, recovery practices, movement, and modern wellness treatments within a calm, refined setting. Today, it stands as an integrative hub for overall wellbeing, supporting balance, longevity, and a more intentional way of living.https://zaazenwellness.com/**FURTHER DETAILS ON 'I LIKE TO MOVE IT, MOVE IT!':LEVEL 1 - ONE MONTH COURSE, September 2026Focus: Body Awareness, Wellbeing & Movement FoundationsA one-month journey for people who don't think of themselves as 'dancers'.Curriculum | What we will explore:•	Body awareness and learning to listen to the body's signals•	Basic anatomy for movement•	Alignment, balance and coordination•	Mobility, strength and movement efficiency•	Breath, energy and presence•	Different ways of moving through space•	Imagination as a tool for movement•	Building confidence and comfort in your own bodyBy the end of the course you will:•	Feel more at home in your body•	Move with greater ease, confidence and freedom•	Develop greater body awareness and self-understanding•	Improve mobility, coordination and physical wellbeing•	Discover new ways of expressing yourself through movement•	Build a strong foundation for further explorationLEVEL 2 (Available to those who have completed Level 1)Focus: Music, Space & Creative ExpressionLevel 2 expands the focus from the inner world to the world around us. Building on the foundations developed in Level 1, participants explore movement in relationship to music, space, objects, imagination and creative expression, while continuing to develop strength, confidence and overall health & wellbeing.Curriculum | What we'll explore:•	Listening and responding to music•	Rhythm, timing and musicality•	Moving in relationship to space and environment•	Working with objects and others•	Improvisation and creative exploration•	Understanding connecting tissues and communicatorsBy the end of the course you will:•	Develop a stronger connection to music and rhythm•	Feel more confident exploring and creating dance/movement•	Expand your expressive and creative range•	Discover new ways of relating to the space and objects around you•	Cultivate mind-body agility and integrated wellbeing•	Experience movement as a source of vitality, expression and play
